/speckit-specify Build a command-line tool for listing and extracting tar archives.

Run it as `python -m tarx COMMAND ...` with two commands:

- `python -m tarx list ARCHIVE` prints the name of every member of the archive, one per line, in the order they appear in the archive.
- `python -m tarx extract ARCHIVE DEST [--overwrite]` extracts the archive's files and directories into the directory DEST, keeping their relative paths and file contents. When it finishes it prints `extracted N files` to standard output, where N is the number of regular files written.

Both plain tar archives (`.tar`) and gzip-compressed tar archives (`.tar.gz` or `.tgz`) must work.

Existing files are never overwritten unless `--overwrite` is given. If extraction would overwrite an existing file and `--overwrite` was not given, the command fails with exit status 3 and an error message on standard error. With `--overwrite`, existing files are replaced.

If ARCHIVE does not exist or is not a valid tar archive, the command prints an error message to standard error and exits with status 2. Successful commands exit with status 0.

Use Python 3.11 or newer and the standard library only. Put the code in a package named `tarx` under `src/`, so that it runs with `python -m tarx` when `src/` is on `PYTHONPATH`.

Examples, for an archive `photos.tar.gz` that contains the files `photos/a.jpg` and `photos/b.jpg`:

```
$ python -m tarx list photos.tar.gz
photos/a.jpg
photos/b.jpg

$ python -m tarx extract photos.tar.gz out
extracted 2 files

$ python -m tarx extract photos.tar.gz out
(an error message on standard error; exit status 3)
```

**What the spec contains:** 3 prioritized, independently testable user stories (P1 extract, P2 list, P3 overwrite control), 14 edge cases, 19 functional requirements, 10 security requirements, 8 measurable success criteria, and an Assumptions section recording every default I chose.

**Two judgment calls worth your attention** — both documented in Assumptions, both cheap to reverse via `/speckit-clarify`:

1. **Archives containing symbolic links, hard links, or special files are refused outright** (exit 2), rather than extracted-with-skipping. Your description promised only "files and directories", and the constitution's Fail Loudly principle rules out silent skipping. The cost: real-world archives that happen to contain a symlink cannot be extracted at all.
2. **Fixed resource bounds** of 10,000 members / 1 GiB total / 1 GiB per member, to stop decompression bombs as the constitution's Security Baseline requires. Not configurable, by Principle IV.

I also had to add a security section your description didn't ask for — constitution Principle V makes a spec with no security requirements ineligible for planning — and I recorded your Python/`src/tarx` constraints as MC-001/MC-002 in a labelled subsection rather than dropping them to satisfy the "no implementation details" checklist item.

**Ready for the next phase**: `/speckit-plan`. Run `/speckit-clarify` first only if you want to revisit either call above.
